text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- a planned merger between state-controlled nuclear firm Framatome and GEC-Alsthom will not take place after Prime Minister Alain Juppe ruled out allowing Britain's GEC to hold more than 50 percent in would-be new unit.
-- Agnelli group may have increased stake in French holiday villages company Club Mediterranee to near 20 percent.
-- Dollar rise boosts European stock exchanges.
-- Retailers such as Carrefour, Casino and possibly Pinault-Printemps-Redoute launch financial services and consumer-credit activities.
-- Markets choose not to link U.S. and European interest rates.
-- Shares in Carbone Lorraine rose by some 6.2 percent yesterday.

-- Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod says in a interview he hopes a merger deal with Suez will be wrapped up on Friday to create a global player called Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux. He wants the group run by a supervisory board in charge of strategy and an executive board headed by Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet.
-- Unions less reluctant to endorsing agreement between government and employers to allow truck drivers to retire at 55 years.
-- Pinault Printemps Redoute chairman Francois Pinault's bid to acquire Bordeaux vineyard Chateau-Ausone rejected by the owner family.
-- Government rebuffs GEC's plans to merge with Framatome.
